author: agent
text:
Re-read after 0.54.0. CORRECTS the confirm below it: PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION is 4, not 3. That earlier confirm recorded "3" as a fact and the number has since moved, which is exactly why the stale flag exists - the rest of that review still holds.

Confirmed true now: PythonParser (parsers.py:66) uses the stdlib ast module with no tree-sitter involvement; tree-sitter appears 13 times in this module but only for the non-Python grammars, which are optional and degrade to a named warning when absent (measured in acceptance: a stranger with no grammars installed gets "javascript: not installed ... fix: pip install 'memway[languages]'", never a traceback).

Why the bump to 4: 0.54.0 changed the shingle hash inside _sketch, and the parse cache PERSISTS sketches. A warm cache would have replayed randomized values forever - the same failure mode as the scope-aware-resolution upgrade that kept serving an old graph until the schema version was introduced. The bump discards the cache wholesale, which is what forces every sketch to be recomputed in one pass.

The inline version history in the constant's comment is the authoritative record of what each bump meant; keep appending to it rather than replacing it.

author: cli
text: Re-read after 0.54.3. CORRECTS the confirm below it: PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION is 5, not 4. Bumped because RawEdge gained via_attr - the parser knows a call was written receiver.name(...) and used to throw that away, and edges.py needs it to refuse resolving an attribute call onto a module-level function. Cached edges predate the field, so the cache had to be discarded wholesale; the inline version history in the constant's comment remains the authoritative record - keep appending to it. Still true: PythonParser uses stdlib ast with no tree-sitter, and the non-Python grammars are optional and degrade to a named warning when absent.

author: cli
text: Re-read after the imported-receiver work. CORRECTS the confirm below: PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION is 6, not 5. Bumped because the Python parser now collects every name bound by an import - module level and function level, which this codebase uses heavily - and qualifies attribute calls whose receiver is one of them. subprocess.run stops being a bare run; query.summary becomes a qualified ref that resolves to our own module. Cached edges predate the qualification, so the cache had to go. Still true: PythonParser uses stdlib ast with no tree-sitter, and the non-Python grammars degrade to a named warning when absent.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.56.0. The module docstring's contract - a language plugin answers what entities exist and how they connect - is unchanged and still describes every parser here. What this release adds is that neither answer spells a reference by hand any more: refs.render produces every disambiguator, in this module and in the registry, so the two halves cannot drift.

author: cli
text:
Re-read at 0.57.2. Module-level comments checked against the code as it stands; the confirms below remain accurate.

What this release added at module level: RawEdge gained TWO fields, and the distinction between them is the thing to preserve. via_attr means 'an attribute call the parser could not resolve to a module' - Python clears it when dst_override qualifies the target. bare means 'no receiver was written at the call site'. They look interchangeable and are not; conflating them dropped rich and sqlalchemy below their corpus recall floors.

Every parser now declares builtin_names. Python's is DERIVED from dir(builtins); Go's and JS's are literal lists from their language specs, which no Python process can introspect; Java's is empty and correct.

PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION went 7 -> 10 in one release, one bump per field or semantic change. Each was necessary rather than cautious: a cache warmed at the previous version replays edges MISSING the new field, which silently disables the rule that reads it instead of failing.

author: cli
text: Re-read at the literal-receiver change. RawEdge now carries THREE call-site facts - bare, via_attr, literal_recv - and the module docstring's account of the parser contract still holds. PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION 10 -> 11: a cache warmed at 10 replays edges with literal_recv=False, which silently disables the rule rather than failing. Fourth bump in this family, same reason each time.

author: cli
text: Re-read at the unparsed-file fix. Module comments unchanged. PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION 11 -> 12: PythonParser now raises on SyntaxError instead of returning ([], []), and a cache warmed at 11 would replay a broken file as an empty one. Fifth bump in this family and the same reason each time - the cache holds behaviour, not just data.
